correctness.rationale: The inner regular n-gon lies in the outer one iff r cos(π/n−θ)≤cos(π/n), because this is the maximal inner support against each outer edge normal. Strict inequality in the other direction exposes exactly n alternating inner vertices; all n unit-radius vertices remain exposed. The shoelace formula yields area n sin(b) max(c,r cos(b−θ)), and cyclic chord lengths yield the two-case perimeter. On the active angle interval, the squared derivative difference factorizes into 2(cos θ−cos(2b−θ))(rT−c)(T−rc)>0, proving both volumes strictly increasing toward θ=b. Direct expansion at r=c gives a linear area excess and quadratic perimeter excess. Independently computed SciPy convex hulls for 585 n,r,θ cases (n=3..11) and agreed for both area and perimeter. Numeric checks corroborate, not substitute for analytic proof.
residual_risks: At r=1,θ=0 vertices coincide; strict onset in θ applies only c<r<1.
